known.title: Not done: `forge lanes --aws setup` refuses a public repo
Functional: AWS setup rejects documented self-hosted Linux runners
Gate: the new AWS controls are absent from the Forge guide
Test: default workflow compatibility and AWS test-group routing
Follow-up: accept the AWS European Sovereign Cloud region

findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 2, Harm 4
Raise: Security
Case: normal use - A developer leaves `GH_REPO` set to a private repo and runs setup in a public checkout. [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_api) resolves the placeholders from `GH_REPO`, so this check reads the private repo and never verifies that its `full_name` matches the checkout's origin. With matching AWS credentials, setup succeeds instead of refusing the public repo. The fake `gh` answers the literal placeholder request and does not exercise this resolution.
findings.title: Not done: `forge lanes --aws setup` refuses a public repo

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - A private repo follows the existing guide's `runner = "self-hosted"` configuration for Linux machines. This prefix check rejects it even though its tests already run on Linux. The suggested change to `ubuntu-24.04` would also move the repo's other jobs away from their existing machines. The supported configuration is documented at `src/forge/templates/skill.md:461`.
findings.title: Functional: AWS setup rejects documented self-hosted Linux runners

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Gate
Case: normal use - An owner asks an agent to enable AWS runners. The shipped guide at `src/forge/templates/skill.md:455` explains `test_runner` but does not name `aws_runners`, the setup command, or the requirement to wait for verified setup before selecting `forge-aws`. The repository's review rule requires a guide or brief update in the same change when a setting or option becomes available. OFF owns the full later guide, but this branch already exposes these controls.
findings.title: Gate: the new AWS controls are absent from the Forge guide

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - The named proof does not establish several claimed outcomes. Its two syncs compare the new workflow with itself, so a stable change from the previous workflow passes; its GitHub call baseline is captured only after init, so extra calls during init are missed. For routing, `test = "echo ok"` cannot be split: `src/forge/quicktest.py:22` and `src/forge/prcheck.py:299` reduce even the `groups = 2` iteration to one group. Finally, checking for both label strings does not establish which runner the expression selects.
findings.title: Test: default workflow compatibility and AWS test-group routing

findings.body:
Gain 2, Work 1, Harm 2
A repo using AWS's `eusc-de-east-1` region is refused as having a malformed setting because this pattern requires the first region component to have exactly two letters. [AWS lists that region](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ec2/latest/instancetypes/ec2-instance-regions.html) and M7i instances there. The refusal occurs before Forge can check the matching account and region.
findings.title: Follow-up: accept the AWS European Sovereign Cloud region
